sentences.text: Ask 1 Candice and Monica are interviewing their first guest about her life story and career.
Listen and write the information in the spaces below.
The first one has been provided as an example.
You now have 30 seconds to study the task.
At the end of the task, you will have one minute to tidy up your answers.
Hello
there everyone in Cyberland.
This is Candace.
And this is Monica.
And we are Extraordinary Hong Kong People.
And our extraordinary guest today is.
Drumroll please. Our extraordinary mother!
Hello mom. Mom.
Oh my! You two are really putting on a show.
Hello to all your viewers.
Now Mom, You have had an extraordinary career but before we get to that let’s find out about your life.
First of all, when did you come to Hong Kong?
I was born in Guangzhou.
But Im not saying when.
And we moved to Hong, Kong.
Hell, When was that again?
It was three years before they started work on Chet Blackcock airport.
that port. _Didn’t they begin building the airport in 1991?
So, three years before then?
Yes, 1988. That was a long time ago.
I was a young girl.
My father your Grandpa Choi moved us to East Point in Hong Kong.
East Point! So, Grandpa Choi has always lived in East Point?
That’s a long time.
I remember him giving us tours of the air traffic control tower when we were little.
It was so exciting.
That’s what I thought too when I was a girl.
And that’s when I fell in love with flying.
And yet you did not follow in Grandpa’s footsteps and become an air traffic controller.
No, I wanted to fly.
But I wasn’t interested interested in planes or jets or airliners or anything like that.
As far back as I can remember, I always wanted to be a helicopter pilot.
But why did you want to be a helicopter pilot specifically?
What's the appeal?
The appeal? Well, gosh, let me see now.
First First of all, I love the noise helicopters make it’s so powerful, Whoop, whoop, whoop, whoop!
Oh Mom, Really?
The noise? You betcha.
So, what’s the other thing?
Well the other thing is being able to land anywhere.
I still think it's amazing.
Anywhere you need to land you can.
But you’re not just a regular helicopter pilot.
pilot, You're a rescue helicopter pilot.
Which brings us to your extraordinary story.
can this? How you and Deadmet is very very romantic, Please share this story with our followers.
Well, I rescued your father in my helicopter.
He was the captain on one of those huge cargo ships.
He was sailing a ship in the Llama Channel when he broke his ankle.
Oh, poor dad!
How did he break his ankle?
Was it in a terrible storm?
Did the ship sink?
Oh, stop it you two.
You know perfectly well what happened.
He fell down some stairs on the ship.
Ha ha ha.
Poor dad. It’s so undramatic, falling down the stairs.
Yes, but if you fell down some stairs and broke your ankle, you wouldn’t be laughing.
laughing? So, what happened after that?
So, did you meet him then when you were flying him to the hospital?
Of course not.
I only saw him then but I didn’t speak to him.
I was flying the helicopter.
Besides, that would be completely unprofessional.
I know, I know.
You are very professional, mum.
Thank you for noticing.
So, actually, actually it was about a year after I rescued him when I first spoke to him.
You see I joined a rock climbing club.
Your father and I were in the same group of beginners.
So, what happened?
Did you rescue him again at the rock climbing club?
No, we were both good at rock climbing.
What actually happened was when I told him I flew rescue helicopters, he told me about his accident and we quickly put two and two together.
And we were the result!
More was the pity.
Anyway, it wasn’t love at first sight.
He was so shy back then.
It was a few months after joining the rock climbing club that I asked him out on a date.
Then it was love.
It was so funny because I asked him out when we were on top of a cliff.
I'm not sure if he looked nervous because I asked him out, out or because we were on top of a cliff.
But he said yes.
